content.rendered:
1969: Bruce plays his first ever show in California, at the Esalen Institute in Big Sur. He unexpectedly encounters a Freehold friend, Richard Blackwell, who sits in with the band during their New Years Eve gig.

1975: Bruce and the E Street Band wrap up 1975 with a magnificent show at Philadelphia’s Tower Theater. Fans in attendance don’t realize it, but they’re witnessing the last “Does This Bus Stop at 82nd Street?” for 18 years, the last “Mountain of Love” for 33 years, and the last slow arrangement of “Tenth Avenue Freeze-Out” for 15 years. This show is available as part of Bruce’s official archive series.

1977: Bruce and the E Street Band join Southside Johnny and The Asbury Jukes on stage at the Capitol Theater in Passaic to close out 1977 in style. Bruce and the boys stick around to play a few songs of their own, including a “Backstreets” performance that leads off with the very first prototype of “Drive All Night” in a one-time-only arrangement.

1978: Bruce and the E Street Band play their last show of the year in Richfield, Ohio. It’s also the second-to-last show of the Darkness Tour, featuring the last “Pretty Flamingo” for 25 years. Shortly after midnight, boisterous fans start lighting off firecrackers, one of which hits Bruce. Steve in particular does not take kindly to this. (Bruce is only a little more restrained.)

1980: Bruce and the boys close out the year with one of their most legendary, most documented and most bootlegged shows, at the Nassau Coliseum in Uniondale. Stretching out over four hours (including the intermission), the set list features 38 songs, including the live premiere of “Held Up Without a Gun” (played because it’s short and the band has a little time to kill before midnight) and the last “Rendezvous” for 19 years. This show will be officially released decades later as part of Bruce’s official archive series. In addition, “Rendezvous” will be released 18 years later on Tracks; “4th of July, Asbury Park (Sandy)” will be released on Live 1975-85; “Merry Christmas, Baby” will be released on A Very Special Christmas; and “Held Up Without a Gun” will be released on The Essential Bruce Springsteen. Whew! But that’s not all: a few songs are captured on 8mm film–watch those highlights below.

1982: Steve Van Zandt marries Maureen Santoro, and Bruce serves as best man. At the reception, Bruce, the E Street Band, Southside Johnny, and Gary U.S. Bonds join the wedding band for six songs including Bruce’s own “I’m a Rocker” and “Hungry Heart.”

1987: Tunnel of Love is certified double platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America.

2020: Bruce calls into E Street Radio and chats with host Jim Rotolo.

excerpt.rendered: Highlights from New Years Eve shows across the years, including the earliest known prototype of “Drive All Night.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 7
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce plays his second album start-to-finish for the first time, debuts a new arrangement for "Blinded by the Light," and plays a last-ditch rally for Hillary Clinton on Election Eve.

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 24
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This date in Springsteen history gave us some gems: check out the unreleased 1980 concert video from Largo, listen to highlights from Bruce's trio of Asbury Park concerts in 1996, and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: December 29
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Bruce's first show in Ohio, performances destined for Live 1975-85, and an E Street Band guest appearance on Good Morning America. More highlights inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 26
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Bruce makes a guest appearance with Patti Smith, debuts "Hearts of Stone," and records a Christmas greeting for Ed Sciaky. Plus: a very crowded "solo" stage in Asbury Park and much more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: December 16
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: It's the debut of "Brothers Under the Bridge," the release of "The Wrestler," and the last "Crush on You" for 28 years as Bruce's tours start to wind down for the year.

jetpack-related-posts.title: November 10
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Not one but *two* Springsteen box sets were released on this date: Live 1975-85 and Tracks. Plus: a Billy Joel guest appearance, a Daily Show interview, and more.
